intro: Searching for a patent lawyer near you usually means you have an invention or a design you want to protect, and you want someone local you can talk to about it. You may be unsure whether you need a patent attorney or an IP solicitor, or what the next step is. iComply can introduce you to a suitable UK professional who will quote you directly, with the price on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a patent lawyer near me usually need
need_lead: Most people behind this search are at the very start of protecting an idea and want clear guidance before they disclose anything.
needs: You have come up with a new product or process and want to know whether it could be patentable before you tell anyone about it.
You have already described your invention to a manufacturer, investor or friend and are worried this may affect your chances of protecting it.
You want help drafting and filing a patent application correctly so it stands the best chance of being accepted.
You have a patent already and need advice on enforcing it or responding to someone who claims you have infringed theirs.
You want to understand how a patent fits alongside other protection such as trade marks or registered designs for your business.
context_heading: Before you speak to anyone, keep your invention confidential
context: Publicly disclosing an invention before filing can undermine its novelty, which is central to whether a patent can be granted. That means holding back from posting details online, showing prototypes at exhibitions or discussing the idea openly until you have taken advice. A professional can carry out searches to help assess novelty and advise on timing.

Patent attorneys are regulated by IPReg, while solicitors in England and Wales are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority and you can check an individual or firm on its register. The word "lawyer" is not protected on its own, so it is worth confirming that whoever handles your matter is a solicitor, a patent attorney or another authorised professional. Regulated firms must hold professional indemnity insurance and have a complaints procedure.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe in general terms what your invention or idea relates to, without disclosing the confidential details themselves.
Say whether you have already filed any application or hold a granted patent, and in which country.
Explain whether you have shared the idea with anyone, such as a manufacturer, investor or business partner.
Mention whether you are an individual inventor, part of a small business or working with others, as this can affect who the professional advises.
Say where you are based and how far you are willing to travel, since you searched for someone near you.
Note whether your enquiry is about filing, enforcing a patent or responding to a claim of infringement, so the right kind of professional is introduced.
questions: Are you a registered patent attorney or a solicitor, and which regulator covers your work?
How will you assess whether my invention is novel before any application is filed?
What information and materials will you need from me to start drafting an application?
How do you charge for the work, and will you confirm the price on application before starting?
What should I avoid doing publicly while an application is being prepared?
If someone later infringes my patent, how would you approach enforcement?

faqs.q: Should I speak to a patent attorney or an IP solicitor?
faqs.a: Patent attorneys specialise in drafting and prosecuting patent applications, while IP solicitors often handle disputes and enforcement. Many matters need both skills, so it helps to explain your situation and let the professional advise on the right fit. iComply can introduce you to a suitable UK professional who quotes you directly.

faqs.q: Can I talk about my invention before filing?
faqs.a: It is generally wise not to disclose an invention publicly before filing, as this can affect novelty. A professional can advise on what counts as disclosure and whether any confidentiality agreement is needed before you speak to manufacturers or investors.

faqs.q: How do I check that someone is properly regulated?
faqs.a: Patent attorneys are regulated by IPReg, and solicitors in England and Wales can be checked on the Solicitors Regulation Authority's register. In Scotland and Northern Ireland the relevant law societies regulate solicitors. Confirming this before you share confidential details is a sensible step.

faqs.q: What does price on application mean here?
faqs.a: It means the professional will quote you directly once they understand your matter, rather than a fixed price being shown in advance. The cost can vary with the complexity of the invention and the work involved. You can ask for the quote and scope in writing before anything begins.
